title: Quarantine the bars cut short against the master sample
instruction: Check the four steel bars in the black tray against the master bar on the white plate. Bars as long as the master go in the grey line tray; any bar shorter than the master goes in the red quarantine bin. Lay each bar flat, and leave the master where it is.
context: After a saw or cut-off setup, operators check parts against a master sample and segregate any nonconforming part so it cannot reach the next operation or the customer (ISO 9001 clause 8.7, control of nonconforming outputs). The decision comes from a side-by-side comparison with the master, not from a colour or label. Shipping a short bar is worse than scrapping a good one, so an escape caps the score. Unlike TK-3WZ2X7 (pins sorted by whether they drop into a go/no-go gauge pocket), the comparison here is visual, against a reference part. Unlike TK-69K78G (pick spacers of a stated length against a ruler), no length is given: each bar is judged against the master and the bad ones are segregated. Done by: inspectors, testers, sorters and saw operators (O*NET 51-9061.00, 51-4031.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table. Incoming tray: a fixed black open frame (walls 0.6 cm thick, 1.5 cm tall, round a 12 x 23 cm pocket) centred at x 20, y 22. In it, four loose steel bars 1.6 cm wide and 1.2 cm tall lying flat along x, 5 cm apart at y 14.5, 19.5, 24.5 and 29.5, their near ends all on the line x 16: the first and third are 8 cm long (120 g), the second and fourth 6 cm (90 g), from a wrong-cut lot. Inspection plate: a fixed white plate 12 x 5 cm, 4 mm thick, centred at x 20, y 38.5, carrying the fixed master bar, 8 cm long, same section, near end on x 16. Line tray: a fixed grey open frame of the same walls round a 12 x 14 cm pocket centred at x 37, y 17. Quarantine bin: the same in red, centred at x 37, y 37.
scoring: From a top photo and a ruler, with the grippers open. A bar is in a tray when it is still, its centre inside the tray's inner walls and its lowest point less than 2.5 cm above the table. 0.25 for each 8 cm bar in the line tray and each 6 cm bar in the quarantine bin. If any short bar is in the line tray, the score is capped at 0.25. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: both full-length bars in the line tray and both short bars in the quarantine bin, held 1 s.
reset_notes: Lay the four bars back in the incoming tray on their marks, near ends on the stop line, the short ones second and fourth.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The bars are plain rectangular sections with square-cut ends and no burrs; the 20 mm length difference is the only defect. The master bar is fixed to its plate. Trays and bin are fixed open frames.
